utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If necessary, I can ask the witness whether that is the way things were done based on his own experience, if the family would not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On the basis that the witness agreed to the content of the document, this document can be admitted. Mr. Karadzic could have spent more time exploring the witness's knowledge about this but in terms of time, the Chamber is of the view to admit this document at the moment. This is admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1697, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3495 -- 1D3945 actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this. It is identical, I hope that there is a translation. Yes. Here comes the translation. Do you remember that on 12 May, the provisional government of Zvornik passed an order on prohibiting the serving of alcoholic beverages? And do you agree that that was -- no, no, no, not this document. We need a different document in Serbian. Actually, it's the same number but the second half. Thank you. That's it. So on 12 May, the serving of alcoholic beverages was prohibited. As a policeman, did you know that, and was that done with a view to decreasing dangers for citizens?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew about that, and the order was being carried out by the police station as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1698, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3946. Can we have that now, please? Can we have the right-hand side where the ERN number is? Can we have that in an enlarged version? Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that had to do with taverns. Do you agree that this order dated 1 June 1992 is related to the selling of alcoholic beverages in shops? And that there is a threat in Article 3, namely failure to carry out this order shall be punished by closing the shop? So in addition to not serving alcoholic beverages in taverns, alcoholic beverages were still a problem and that's why the government passed this decision not allow the selling of alcoholic beverages in shops either, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We admitted it, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. It will be given a separate number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1699, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now we are going to have 1700. 3949. Could we have that number, please? And that is going to be Defence Exhibit 1700. 1D3949.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that at some point in time, in the beginning of July, a new order was issued on prohibiting the bringing of weapons into the town of Zvornik, and that pertained both to uniformed and non-uniformed persons? So could the Serbian version please be enlarged for the witness? The right-hand part of that page. No, not the left one, the right one. Yes, thank you. Do you agree that this measure was introduced because there was lots of weaponry all over, in the hands of the paramilitaries and in the hands of other persons, and therefore they did not allow the carrying of weapons and the public security and the military police of Zvornik were in charge of seizing such weapons, just like in the Wild West, right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, we had a few problems with military personnel who did not want to hand over weapons to the police, and then we would inform the military police about that and then they would come and take their weapons from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Exhibit D1700.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3948, can we have that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A moment ago you mentioned that Zuca had intended to take over the municipality building along with the administration; right? And that that was a real danger; right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, yes, exactly, that's what I wanted to have enlarged. Do you agree that that is probably the reason why, on 2 July, the provisional government did not allow weapons to be brought into the Municipal Assembly building, right? Do you remember this order? And do you link it up with these intentions of the paramilitaries to take the Municipal Assembly, the building of the Municipal Assembly, that is?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that, and I think that that is why the order was issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1701, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D3951?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At one point in time, the president of the Executive Board was Radosav Peric, the deputy head of the provisional government. Actually, it was no longer the provisional government. It was the Executive Board by then; right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at this order again. It is repeated and it's spelled out in more specific terms. It is dated 24 September, yet again there is this ban on bringing weapons into the town of Zvornik, and that that pertains to persons in uniform and persons not wearing uniform and Article 2 says that the only exceptions are authorised officials of the MUP, the military police, and soldiers if they are moving through town in an organised manner and under command. And your station and the military police were entrusted with the implementation of this order. Do you remember this order?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and we enforced it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Exhibit D1702.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 25564. 2564. 02564. Could we now zoom in on this page, with the ERN number, the one on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is 29 June, a conclusion of the provisional municipal government, that uniforms may be issued only to -- only by authorisation from the commander of the Zvornik Brigade and do you agree that this is an attempt to prevent unauthorised wearing of uniforms around the municipality? Do you recall this order, this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember all sorts of people were wearing all sorts of uniforms. Everyone brought them from their own native place, from their units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1703, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3952, please. Could we display this page a bit larger, with the ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that on 12 November, Radoslav Peric as president of the Executive Board wrote a recommendation to the police to review the active duty and the reserve police personnel, the second paragraph says that all employees of the police who are inclined to engage in inappropriate conduct, all those who joined paramilitary units and who left the Serbian army to join other units in other places, should be expelled? Do you recall this recommendation?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember it. A large number of members of the police were sent to serve in the army at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They did not like it very much. They were not fit for the police, and they could do less damage in the army; right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And they were closer to combat in the army. Most of them had done only police work until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we say that this process of purging the police continued, it was not uncommon at that time to be expelled from the police? In other words, you did not tolerate on your force people who were not fit for police work?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see -- can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1704, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D3957. We are now moving to the subject of property protection and property issues, on which various decisions and orders were made. Could we display to the witness the left side, without the ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You see this order. Boards of management may dispose of socially owned apartments in their own property, and occupancy rights may not be modified, and abandoned apartments can only be decided upon by the provisional government. This was designed to prevent any handling of property in illegal ways, to prevent abuse and squatting and inappropriate use of business and residential premises.

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Early on, there was a lot of unauthorised eviction, but after this order, a panel was established to allocate abandoned apartments to displaced persons from the federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On a temporary basis; right? Such apartments were returned, were restored to the rightful owner, after the war?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Zvornik, I believe 100 per cent of all property was returned to the owners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1705, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see 1D3963? Can we concentrate on the left page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 9 September. The president of the Executive Board, Mr. Peric, renders null and void all contracts on the lease of business premises concluded after 6 April 1992, between physical persons and the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik. This -- all this fishing in muddy waters that went on before this decision is what the president of the Executive Board tried to stop?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1706, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3950 is the document I would like to call up next. Page 2, or, rather, the side with the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in this document, on 17 July, the provisional government banned the resettlement of Serbs who had fled from Kladanj, Kalesija and Zivinice in the town of Zvornik, and this does not apply to the families of fallen fighters. Article 3 says that these refugees are not allowed to become permanent residents but instead they have to register with the secretariat for the admission of refugees. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1707, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3960, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: We can call up the document, Your Honour, but I think this may be a duplicate of 1D3948 that we've already dealt with and has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown the right-hand side with the ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned yourself that there was a lot of malfeasance with the real estate, immovable property, et cetera. Do you recall that on 17 July, the temporary -- the provisional government issued an order ordering the secretariat for the admission of refugees, and the public security station, to form a commission to supervise the occupancy and use of family housing facilities, to inspect all occupied apartments, and to immediately evict any unauthorised occupants? You remember this? There was a lot of squatting at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And we also discussed the establishment of this commission earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So this was not a duplicate of what we admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: I believe it is, Your Honour. It's just that with 1D3948 Mr. Karadzic focused on the left side and on this one he is focused on the right side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is the right side of that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which seems to be a separate document and the English translation is uploaded on a separate --

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Okay, for that reason, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will admit that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D1708, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3955, please. Could we focus on the left side in the box?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the commission that was referred to? "A commission is hereby formed to inspect the use of socially owned flats." Do you know these people listed here?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's one of the commissions. The composition later changed. I know Rade Vukic, I know Tomo Jasic, Aleksandar Kusic, Slobodan Krstanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when people illegally moved into an apartment, your Public Security Service would come and assist where necessary?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1709, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3958, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a separate document referring to property issues and how they were governed. This is a decision - isn't it? - made on 22 June, outlining criteria for provisional accommodation in abandoned apartments and family houses, and Article 2 says, temporary occupancy, it stipulates exactly who is entitled to occupy these residences temporarily, and do you recall this? Do you remember that this was specifically defined as temporary occupancy of abandoned apartments and family houses?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that. I think that even some old-timers got these apartments to use for a while, those whose own homes had been destroyed in war operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1710, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, do I have any more time? We have one more topic to cover. The efforts to restore the rule of law, to make the municipality operate as a state within the state, considering that it was cut off from central authorities. And we can corroborate this with documents. Mr. Panic is very well-versed in state administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have about half an hour after the break. We'll have a break now for an hour and resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now please have 1D3661 in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to show you some documents that you were aware of because of your post, where we have instances where the municipality acted as a state within a state, and this was confirmed here. Now, would you agree with me if I said that within our old system the municipality was rather independent and autonomous in view of its functions, national defence and many others? Do you recall that there was a lot of autonomy within municipalities?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look now at one of the decisions dated 22 April, in other words after the first conflict broke out. The provisional government is issuing a decision on forming a single organisation for the provision of health care services, and unifying the general hospital, health centre and pharmacy, and transforming them into a single organisation in Zvornik. Now, would you agree with me that there is then a list of the names of the persons who were part of the management board, including Jelkic Muhamed, who was a surgeon I believe, an internist, a Muslim by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Muhamed Jelkic. Was -- had a specialisation in internal medicine and he stayed in Zvornik for perhaps a month or two longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He was not an extremist and he was welcome in his various posts and functions, he was also appointed as a member of the Crisis Staff, which was Serbian and Muslim, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was an expert in his field. He was a very good doctor and he had that reputation both among the Serbs and the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But would you agree with me that this would be a function of ministries, not municipalities, in other words reorganising and transforming the structures of health care institutions?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the early days of the conflict, perhaps because of the breakdown of communications, municipalities took it upon themselves to take decisions on various aspects of activity which sometimes were not within their authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1711, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now have 1D3969, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that those municipalities that were cut off had a sense that they were left to their own devices?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please take a look here at a decision whereby judges in the lower court are relieved of their duties and if you look at the list, I was able to count six Serbs and five Muslims on the list, if Tiric is a Muslim; the fifth name is Serb; 8th is Serb; 9 is a Serb, Petar Ristic; 10 Vaso, a Serb; 11, Milenko, a Serb; and 13, Dragan, a Serb.

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Zlatko Tiric was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, seven Serbs and six Muslims. Now, would you agree with me that many people left and were relieved of their duties because they were no longer there. We can't really see what the reason for it -- this is. For their being relieved of duty here.

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And -- yes, people of both ethnicities were leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1712, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 1D3974, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you see that this is a decision to appoint the secretary of the holding centre for refugees issued on 4 June? This would be something that would fall within the purview of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I can answer that question but I do know that this person, Cedo Kojic was appointed to that post.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see the second half of this document in Serbian, where we see that judges are appointed to lower courts, to the municipal court in Zvornik. We see that this is an appointment of Radovan Nikolic as a judge of the municipal court. Can we agree that appointments of judicial positions -- to judicial positions was something that was within the purview of the government?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we -- I'd like to tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1713, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see 1D3975, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that here we see that on 22 June, approval is given for -- my apologies. This is not so relevant. Could we have the next page, please? These are financial documents, so we are not really interested in that but can you see here that we have the approval of the appointment of the chief of the Defence Ministry department in the municipality, and it was proposed and approved that Stevan Ivanovic should be appointed to that duty. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And just to add, this too is the function of the Ministry of Defence, it's within the purview of the Ministry of Defence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's how it should be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it would appear that his appointment was extended, that he had been appointed on 15 March and here approval is given for extending his post or rather his appointment to that post; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D1714.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see 1D3976, please? Can we see the left-hand side, the one that doesn't bear the ERN number? Could you just zoom in on that for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that here the municipality is even appointing the military prosecutor, and that this is something that could not be the case under normal circumstances? This is not something for the municipality to do; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The municipality could -- would not be able to do that, especially not appoint a military prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1715, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that up until 8 July, this provisional government is in existence? We see that the person signing for it is Branko Grujic, correct? And then if we look at the next document, 1D3977, we can see that it's already Mr. Pejic. Could we have 1D3977? Can we zoom in on the left-hand side of the B/C/S version, the one without the ERN number? Now, please look at this. Would you agree that this decision is a decision where the new prime minister decides to reinstate the functions of the normal municipal government, and it says here that those organs that had been elected before the coming into effect of the declaration on the state of war will remain in force, and that up until the chairman of the Executive Committee is elected, Radosav Peric would be at the head of the interim government and this too coincides with the time when the paramilitaries were arrested; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On 20 July already, Branko Grujic had resigned and been replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Mr. Peric here assessed that there are no longer reasons for the provisional work of the government and that the regular government bodies should be reinstated that had not functioned up until then; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I see on top that it says that on 20 July, Grujic was appointed -- was relieved of duties but in fact it should be 28 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the preamble it says, at a session held on 28 July 1992, perhaps it's not visible enough, and at the bottom, too, we see the date of 28 July 1992. So that's exactly on the same day when the arrest occurred; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Gogic's group was expelled on the night of 27/28 July, whereas the special unit expelled the Zuca's men on the 29th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1716, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now see 1D3978, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that as of that day, 28 July, law and order is being reinstated in the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the arrest of these paramilitary forces, there was a change in the leadership of the municipality as well as the SUP. So that the rule of law was reinstated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on 19 August we can see here there is a decision to establish a municipal prison for the municipalities of Bratunac, Zvornik and Skelani, and the seat should be in Zvornik. Was this a prison that was meant for criminal acts, for criminals, criminal perpetrators of criminal acts, not for prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this implemented, this decision?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1717, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This too would be within the purview of the Ministry of Justice, but the communications with the central government were still not fully in place; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now see 1D3979? This decision is on the appointment of a commission for prisoner exchanges. Did you know that there was such a commission established, that these people were its members, and that Slavoljub Tomasevic was its president and one of the members was a doctor, the name under number 7, correct?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't have an opportunity to see this decision earlier, but I know that I know both Dr. -- Mr. Tomasevic and Dr. Umicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that the Muslim side frequently reneged on the agreement to exchange prisoners and also the exchanges of civilians and soldiers who had been killed?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Very often there were delays.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that Captain Dragan intended to get a killed policeman out, or someone else, a policeman I think from Kamenica. Do you remember that, often, in Kamenica and in other places where there were Muslim concentrations, killed fighters were massacred, mutilated, and that this horrified the population, they impaled them, they cut off their heads, and circumcised them, as is done in some religions?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that the late Slavko Eric, when he was taken out, certain parts of his body had been torn off and burned, I don't know about the rest. I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Elliott?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour I don't have, again, a problem with admitting the document but all the witness did was confirm that he knew two of the people listed. He didn't comment on the -- this commission or this document in any other way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He didn't ask about the content of this document. Would you like to ask further questions, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I'd just like to ask or rather I did ask that he asked whether a commission existed and he said that he did know and that he knew two men and he knew the commission had a problem with carrying out the agreed exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is my understanding correct, Mr. Peric -- or rather, Mr. Panic, Peric is the signatory?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I haven't seen the document but I heard of this commission, and I know not only two people but I also know the late Cvijan Rakic and Tomasevic and Dr. Umicevic and Lazar Pejic. I knew all of them actually, as far as the commission was concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Elliott?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Ms. Elliott, can you assist us here, please? The question Dr. Karadzic asked was this: [As read] "You mentioned that Captain Dragan intended to get a policeman out or someone else, a policeman I think from Kamenica. Do you remember that often in Kamenica and other places where there were Muslim concentrations, killed fighters were massacred, mutilated, and that this horrified the population, they impaled them, they cut off their heads and circumcised them as is done in some religious?" And he said yes. Now, would that yes govern the question asked, would you say?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: I would say that the witness then qualified and said what he was assenting to, and that was he knew about the late Slavko Eric and he heard about other things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you think that yes didn't -- had no bearing on the actual question, in that he agreed with the question, that yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: I would not understand that yes to be that he adopted all aspects of Mr. Karadzic's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much indeed. Mr. Witness, you were asked a question by Dr. Karadzic. I read it out a while ago but I shall read it again for you. He asked: "You mentioned that Captain Dragan intended to get a policeman killed -- killed policeman out or someone else, a policeman I think from Kamenica. Do you remember that, often, in Kamenica, and in other places, where there were Muslim concentrations, killed fighters were massacred, mutilated, and then this horrified the population, they impaled them, they cut off their heads and circumcised them as is done in some religions." And you said yes. What did that "yes" mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, Captain Dragan did not go to Kamenica. People said that he was brought in in order to go to Kamenica to get the dead bodies of the killed policemen from there including the late Slavko Eric. I know Slavko Eric, when he was taken out his body had been burned, that was established, and I know that at the hill of Glodjani over 60 Serbs were killed. Some were found without certain parts of their body. Others haven't even been found yet. As for myself, seeing this, no, I have not seen this myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The text does not include what the witness said namely that the bodies had been dismembered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: The question was: [As read] "They were massacred, mutilated, and that this horrified the population and they impaled them, they cut off their heads and circumcised them as is done in some religions." Thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, that's an example of showing the problem of compound questions. In relation to this document itself, you also asked, I quote line 7, page 62: [As read] "This decision is on the appointment of a commission for prisoner exchange. Did you know that there was such a commission established? That these people were its members? And that Slavko Tomasevic was its president and one of the members was a doctor, the name under 7; correct?" And if he says yes, we are not sure, yes to what? So please refrain from making compound questions. But on the basis of the answers, we will admit this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1718, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I just have three documents left and a question. And then we show the map and then we are done. Can we have 1D3970? Your Excellencies, I accept this criticism. However, I do my best to finish as much as possible within the time allocated to me, and that is probably where I err. Can we enlarge the page where the ERN number is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this decision speaks about the establishment of a special unit of the Territorial Defence on 18 April while the JNA was still there in a legal manner? Also, it's a bit too much to have a municipality pass a document like this; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1719, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D3972, can we have that, please? The page where the ERN number is, could that please be zoomed in for the witness, in Serbian? I believe that there is a translation, though. The witness just needs the right-hand side of the document. Oh, I am sorry, there is no translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that here on 25 May this same Mr. Grujic is postponing the implementation of this decision, that's what he says? I beg your pardon, no, no. This actually -- this actually has to do with physical, legal persons who have accounts in Serbia. They have to return their money so that they would be under the control of the tax authorities. Do you agree that this conclusion pertains to that?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what is written here that is what it says but I don't really know much about things like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that they are trying to regulate the financial system too, as if they were the state itself, and that this is a result of this isolation of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The witness answered that he doesn't really know much about things like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 15345? 15345 is the 65 ter number. Could I have that page, please, the one that has an ERN number, can that be zoomed in for the witness? I believe that there is a translation. This document was on the Prosecution list. No. There is no translation yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree here that on 11 May Mr. Grujic is delaying the implementation of the decision? Do you agree that this would correspond to the lack of enthusiasm on the part of the JNA to have yet another unit formed in its area of responsibility? Do you remember that this unit was not established?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know of this conclusion. I had not seen it. And the unit was not established. I don't know anything else about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be admitted? It can be added to the other one when the decision was made, and then there is this decision not to have it established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1720, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Panic, the Prosecutor asked you whether you knew anything about Srebrenica, and they asked you about the visit of General Subotic. Is it correct that you don't know anything about any of these things that happened in relation to Srebrenica? And is it correct that you do not know that General Subotic asked about graves with a view to destroying evidence? That is what you stated in the transcript of your interview with the Prosecution, the year is 2002, and the pages are 57 and 58, right?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right that I don't know anything about Srebrenica. I was not in Srebrenica at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in Zvornik, people did not know much about what was happening in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zvornik, everything that had anything to do with Srebrenica was taken over by the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for Subotic, you did not hear about him trying to destroy anything or hush things up or anything else?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't even know this Subotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now ask for 1D4275? We'd like to ask you to mark some things for us briefly on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you give the reference for your question about the Prosecutor asking whether he knew anything about Srebrenica? Did you mean in examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was in the examination-in-chief or in the transcript. And here we have this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your interview, yes, now I have understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, could we have a reference for that interview? I haven't been able to find what Mr. Karadzic is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 22580, interview dated 17 October 2002, pages 57 and 58.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm not able to see any reference to Srebrenica on pages 57 or 58.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The last question seems to be the -- whether he can tell about visit of Bogdan Subotic, then minister for defence, to Zvornik for the purpose of arranging the reburial of the killed people. Can you move to the next page? Were you referring to this passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes, yes, but I thought that the OTP was linking that to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Your last question, about map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the map in e-court? The OTP was kind enough to have it uploaded. It was hard for us because the format was rather big. Although they have been kind we do have to note that there is no equality of arms. They can do what we cannot. 1D4275. We will be using it often, so once we have admitted it then we will be able to call it up often. It's coming. Thank you. Could you please zoom in on Zvornik? That is on the right-hand side, the upper third of the map, a bit to the north. Right there. For all the participants, this is a map of the geography institute. This is the ethnic distribution, the borders of municipalities and then the smaller ones are the borders of villages and hamlets. And the census is 1981, the one that is not controversial because it was passed in the assembly. Can we just enlarge the municipality of Zvornik? Can we actually just have the municipality of Zvornik on our screens? It's on the very edge there, the second one from the top on the right-hand side. Precisely. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you -- actually, can we please keep it in the centre? Yes, it can be this way as well. Well, tell us, this blue area down there, is that Drinjaca that was cut off from Zvornik? Where Pivarski stayed without you being able to have any insight into what was going on?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably. Most probably, but I'm not sure. I'm not good with maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you agree with that within between this blue area and Zvornik, there lie Kamenica, Cerska and Glodjansko Hill areas that Muslims continued to control until the spring 1993?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everything that is marked green was populated by Muslims, and the blue areas were Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this how the municipalities were supposed to look like, the blue to be Serb municipalities, and the green to be Muslim municipalities?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the politicians agreed, but that's how it is, according to the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just one more thing, do you agree that those green fields to the north-east of the town itself were controlled throughout the war by the Muslim army, Sapna and the other areas, and to this day they remain in the BH federation?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we did not mark anything, we will do it another time. I will not tender this now but I just wanted the participants to have some idea of who lived where. An image. Thank you, witness. I'm sorry I kept you this long but you have helped us shed light on certain things. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Elliott?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Yes, may I please call up 65 ter 13685?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you could just review this document and I'm, in particular, drawing your attention to the reference to the decree of state president Radovan Karadzic where according to this document, you had been awarded a medal for services to the people. What were you awarded this medal for?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I'm wondering how this arises from the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Elliott?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, at line -- page 68 of today's transcript, Mr. Karadzic asked, first of all, a question in relation to what this witness knew about Srebrenica and the witness said he didn't know anything about Srebrenica, and that in Zvornik everything that had anything to do with Srebrenica was taken over by the military. And I have a few documents to show the witness in relation to these questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Ms. Elliott.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: So my question for the witness was: What were the circumstances or why was he awarded this medal for services to the people?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen the reasoning of that decision, but the proposal was made by the ministry and the ministry made it to the president, probably. In any case, I was awarded that medal for, among other things, expelling the paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that in September of 1995, you were awarded a medal in relation to events from 1992? Is that just clear?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think I got this decoration in 1993, not 1995. I'm not sure but I think it was 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: May that document be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Panic, the document says 1995. Could you take a look at it again? Why don't we zoom in, collapse the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's possible, but on the certificate I got, there is no date, so it could well be 1995. And there is one man whose name was stated as Petko Panic, son of Radovan. So his decoration was never even recognised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. This will be admitted. Yes, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President I'm wondering what's the relevance of this document now that you've found that it emanates from cross-examination about Srebrenica events, I don't see how it's relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Relevant to?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Relevant to anything other than the potential credibility of the witness and I don't see that the Prosecutor is trying to impeach the credibility of the witness or say that he's biased in favour of Dr. Karadzic because he gave him this award.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Elliott, would you like to respond?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Well, I think that the witness has given basis to admit the document and I think it does have some relevance to these proceedings in light of the timing of the award.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: But excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could be a bit more specific in relation to your reference to these -- relevance to these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: I believe this Trial Chamber will hear quite some evidence about the activities of Dragomir Vasic and Mane Djuric during Srebrenica component of the case and that this document will have some bearing on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's what I thought, Mr. President. I think that this is really being used as a subterfuge for other things which were not covered in the direct examination. The events of Srebrenica, where Dr. Karadzic made reference to it, the Prosecutor objected and asked for a reference. It turned out what he was referring to didn't relate to Srebrenica. And there was no evidence elicited on cross-examination about 1995 events. Now, what the Prosecution is trying to do is smuggle in documents that deal with those events through a witness who was not examined on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I didn't hear --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just explain something further? This document has not been interpreted correctly. Herein, Mr. Vasic requests fast-track promotion for these people, and one of the arguments he forwards is that they have been decorated at some point already, and the witness is probably right in saying that he got his award in 1993 because it is said here that they have been decorated but not in September 1995. He's just mentioning this decoration in support of their fast-track promotion; is that correct, witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see towards the bottom only now it reads, in view of the above, we propose that the above-mentioned employees be exceptionally promoted to the rank, et cetera, et cetera. That's when I got the rank of Captain First Class, but the original decoration, I believe, was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you also said, witness, that the proposal goes from the chief to the ministry and the ministry submits it to the president. Do you agree that the president does not know these people? He acts based on proposals made from lower levels? Did you and I know each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't. I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, this is not an opportunity for you to put additional questions. Just a question for Mr. Robinson. Then do we have basis to admit this document in relation to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have a basis but no relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will admit this document later on. Not this time, Ms. Elliott. Through another witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Panic, Dr. Karadzic asked you at page 68 about events in Srebrenica, and in particular he said, "And in Zvornik people did not know much about what was happening in Srebrenica." And your answer was: "In Zvornik, everything that had anything to do with Srebrenica was taken over by the military." It's an adjudicated fact in this case that thousands of Bosnian Muslim men from the Srebrenica enclave were executed and buried in different locations in Srebrenica, Bratunac and Zvornik municipalities. You were chief of the Zvornik police station in July 1995. What do you know about the execution of thousands of Bosnian Muslim men from Srebrenica in the Zvornik municipality in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't believe this arises from the direct examination and if it does -- from the cross-examination, if it does, it's going to open up a lot of potential recross-examination, so this is such -- such a broad question as this, what do you know? If the Prosecution wanted to call him for Srebrenica events they should have called him for that in their direct examination, not to take some grain and blow it up into a tornado.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But is it not true that the witness said that everything was taken up by military and then Prosecution is entitled to explore what the witness personally knew? And then, if necessary, the Defence may have some further cross-examination on that point, if --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, if you believe that that is appropriate from that general answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Elliott, we will allow you to ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember the question that I asked of you or would you like me to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No need to repeat. Perhaps I misspoke when I said I knew nothing about Srebrenica. What I meant is I was not in Srebrenica, but there was the 1st Company from our police station in Srebrenica, including the chief, Dragoja Vasic. What I really meant was that what happened in Zvornik, the prisoners were brought to the school in Rocevici and another location, and that was handled by the military.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: If I could call up 65 ter 23195, please. Sir, do you know who is Mile Renovica?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he worked in the State Security Service in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: And I believe you've already clarified your answer in cross-examination about police involvement in Srebrenica, but is this document consistent with your understanding of MUP involvement in the liberation of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PETKO PANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document lists only employees of the State Security Service. They were higher up than me in hierarchy, and a totally different organisational unit. I had no access to that kind of information. That was state security.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Were you -- that's fine. I'll leave that, Your Honour. That concludes my re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Elliott. Do you have any question in relation to the questions and answers put in relation to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing in particular. I could just repeat the question: Did we know each other? Was that decoration granted based on our personal relationship or was it the usual procedure?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That has been answered already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the answer was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then we'll not allow you to put that question. It's not necessary. I'll check the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: You did admit the document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. He answered -- his answer was recorded, line 21 on page 74. I beg your pardon, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I thought that you had admitted the document but perhaps you didn't actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That concludes your evidence, Mr. Panic. On behalf of the -- this Chamber and the Tribunal, I'd like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence also thanks you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is the next witness a protected one?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to adjourn for -- no? There is one matter before we bring in the next witness. Mr. Tieger, with regard to the witness who is scheduled to appear the last for this week, who is a public witness, I think it's safe to name his name, it's Nusret Sivac. It is my information that the Prosecution intends to tender only 38 pages of the witness's prior testimony from the Stakic case, whereas his whole transcript is 427 pages long. Are you aware of this situation and, in the position to explain why? Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll deal with that. It's not my witness but it must be a mistake in the Rule 92 ter notification. Because we would be submitting the entirety of his Stakic transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I would like to just raise a couple of matters, one with respect to this past witness and one related to the next witness, and then after that perhaps in private session with respect to the protective measures for the next witness. But, first of all, just with respect to the time for cross-examination, again, with respect to this last witness, I want to thank Judge Baird for his intervention because I think that is like an ah-hah moment when you see how compound questions can lead to things that don't clarify the proceedings at all, and I know that I myself have asked compound questions from time to time, and it's almost always when I'm in a rush. And I think Dr. Karadzic also tends to ask those kinds of questions near the end of his allotted time, and so while he bears the responsibility and the fault for asking compound questions, I'd like to call the Chamber's attention to ask you to consider giving him the same amount of time in his examination, direct -- cross-examination as the Prosecution has for its direct examination, including the Rule 92 ter materials and we are able to gauge that pretty accurately as opposed to when they have amalgamated statements, when they use transcript from previous proceedings. This prior witness testified for about five and a half hours in the Zupljanin case on direct examination and another hour and a quarter here in this case, for six and three quarters hours. And you gave Dr. Karadzic three and a half hours in which to complete his cross-examination with you I extended but that caused the time pressure and so if you had given him six and quarters hours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, let's be specific could you identify areas or topics about which Mr. Karadzic was not able to cover due to time constraint, in relation to the previous witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think in relation to the previous witness with the extension that he was able to cover most of -- there are some documents I think that make similar points to those that he made, that we left out, but in general he was able to complete, in this instance, his cross-examination but he did have to rush and he committed the fault of asking compound questions in the course of that. So I think if you had given him six and three-quarters hours he would have been happy to finish early for you, and yet without the same kind of time pressure that you put him under for every witness. Which brings me to the next witness: I want to also make a timely application for more time for the next witness. Because he testified in direct examination for seven hours in the earlier case, and is expected to testify for another hour here, making a total of eight hours and you've allocated Dr. Karadzic three and a half hours for his cross-examination. And I think it's been the practice at this Tribunal to at least give the same amount of time as the Prosecution. I don't understand why Dr. Karadzic keeps being allocated such a short amount of time for each witness. And again, he can stop early, he won't have to use all of the time if he doesn't need it, but when you put him under this kind of pressure by restricting his time below that which seems to be reasonable according to the practice of the Tribunal, then I think that we are all suffering from that, not only him but the accurate flow of information to the Trial Chamber. So I would ask you to consider increasing the time allocation for this next witness to eight hours, and if we don't use it all, then we'll all be the better for it. Finally, Mr. President, I would like to go into private session to make a motion with respect to the witness's protective measures. I understand the next witness is to testify entirely in closed session, and we object to that and I'd like to put on the record why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we go -- may the Chamber move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 21st day of September, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.00 p.m.,
